solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

S029-01.notes: Rests on a single ambiguous piece of evidence -> weak/tenuous. Indisputable is the opposite; obsolete and deliberate don't fit.

S029-02.notes: 'Not a sudden breakthrough' + 'only slightly longer' each generation = incremental.

flags: minor: 'as far as 4,000 kilometers' is a little low; most sources cite up to ~4,500-4,800 km (about 3,000 mi). Not answer-affecting.
S029-03.notes: Passage builds to multigenerational migration. B is a detail; C and D unsupported.

S029-04.notes: Dung -> moth eggs -> moths in fur -> nutrients -> algae -> sloth food; descent sustains the cycle. Matches Pauli et al. (2014) hypothesis. D contradicts the benefit; A, B unsupported.

flags: minor: D says 'C averaged 4.6 tons' while table unit is metric tons per hectare and other choices say 'Variety C'/'metric tons per hectare'; slight style inconsistency (and D's shortened form makes it stand out).
S029-05.notes: Claim has two parts: highest average (4.6) and least consistent (range 6.0-2.9=3.1 vs 0.6 for A, 1.3 for B). Only D addresses both; A is the tempting half-answer. Arithmetic checks.

S029-06.notes: Text 2 shows soloists reuse pre-practiced licks, contradicting 'nothing prepared in advance.' B is the opposite; C contradicts Text 2; D unsupported.

S029-07.notes: Nonessential appositive 'a mathematician by training' opened with a comma must close with a comma. Dash mismatches; semicolon splits subject from verb; no punctuation leaves appositive unclosed. Ada Lovelace's 1843 notes on the Analytical Engine: factually accurate.

S029-08.notes: Two independent clauses with no conjunction -> semicolon. Comma = comma splice; ', which' is ungrammatical; ': and' is nonstandard double punctuation.

flags: minor: one could argue 'Similarly' (both look ahead in the reading direction), but 'In contrast' fits the right-vs-left emphasis and is clearly best.
S029-09.notes: Right vs. left direction contrasted. Eye-movement perceptual span asymmetry for Hebrew/Arabic is well documented (Pollatsek et al., 1981).

S029-10.notes: Only D generalizes; A-C are single-species specifics. Facts (serotinous lodgepole/jack pine cones, eucalyptus epicormic buds) are accurate.
